From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Park <elena@torchwell.ai>
Date: 2027-07-01T10:08:00Z
Subject: RE: Torchwell Dedicated sizing — tokens/sec -> GPU lattice

Folks — I pulled the numbers into a quick model and sketched a sizing diagram (see sizing_diagram_v1.png). Summary and assumptions: 
- Model: LlamaX-13B, quantized int4, perf baseline: ~1.2 tokens/sec per GPU core-equivalent for 1024 context under our runtime; effective per-GPU throughput ~1,800 tokens/sec when fully allocated with batching.
- Cold-start/warm-up KV cache: initial requests pay a ~15% latency penalty for the first ~30s per model shard.
- For Torchwell peak bursts (~2,800 tokens/sec regional), safe production fit requires: 
  * Primary slab: 2 x A40-equivalent GPUs (hot pool) delivering ~3,600 tokens/sec aggregate for the model variant (covers p95 target with margin).
  * Safety lattice: 1 additional warm spare (pre-warmed, lower power mode) to absorb model reloads and micro-surge.
  * Autoscale headroom: we recommend policy to allow short 90s bursts to spill to a compatible cheaper quantized variant (LlamaX-13B-8q) if cold-warm reclamation exceeds threshold.
- p95 latency mapping: with primary slab above and KV caching, expected p95 ~380-420ms at 1024. With safety lattice active, p95 worst-case ~500ms for very short spikes (meets Elena's tolerance).
- Tokens/day math: primary slab handles baseline comfortably; risk window is concurrent multi-hour sustained spikes — propose a monthly burst allowance (tokens) contract.

Action items:
1) Ben — can we map this to commit tiers and cost delta for 2+1 slab + burst allowance?
2) Tessa — confirm POC window (6 weeks) and whether Torchwell needs on-prem or VPC first.
3) Elena — any constraints on fallback variant quality (we should quantify output regression for 8q).

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
